jobs.description: Manager, Service Delivery This job provides strategic leadership in the delivery of child and family programs, drawing on deep expertise in the ministry’s operational and legislative frameworks. This role fosters a client-centered, high-performing culture and leads the development of plans, initiatives, and strategies that promote a high-quality, culturally responsive child welfare system aligned with the ministry’s goals. Building and maintaining strong partnerships with First Nations and other community organizations is a key component of this role. This job is a middle manager role. Middle managers have a critical role in employee engagement and the culture of our organization. The role requires leadership in translating and cascading strategic direction into operational actions, contributing to the achievement of organizational goals. The role is also responsible for delivering on personal work objectives, as well as the work of others for whom they have supervisory responsibilities.

jobs.title: Emergency Duty Worker
jobs.description: Emergency Duty Worker This job delivers critical after-hours services to children and families in crisis, ensuring the safety, stability, and well-being of children in out-of-home care. The role supports families in safely caring for their children by providing responsive, innovative, and accountable services. Responsibilities include investigating child abuse and neglect referrals, assessing safety risks, and developing intervention and safety plans tailored to each family's needs. The role requires travel and includes transporting children and families as part of service delivery.

jobs.title: Fire Base Supervisor This supervisory job is responsible for providing leadership, supervision, and performance assessment for direct reports, contract fire crews, and emergency fire fighters. The role encompasses organizing and coordinating both tactical and strategic fire suppression responses within the forest protection area. In addition to suppression efforts, the Supervisor oversees wildland fire pre-suppression activities such as maintaining equipment and infrastructure, procuring goods and services, planning fire response strategies, delivering public education, mitigating fire risks, and ensuring employees receive the training necessary to meet operational and safety standards. Requirements include travel, on-call availability, and working in challenging conditions such as extreme heat and smoke. Supervisors may also be temporarily assigned to other locations, including out-of-province or international postings, to support forest protection operations.
